{"search_note":"I did not find a 2024 national household survey or administrative dataset showing broad year-end gains in actual access to health, education, water, sanitation, housing, food security, or social protection.

The best pro-evidence is mostly about launches, budgets, and targeted programs, not completed nationwide outcomes.

Evidence is especially thin on housing and formal social protection scale-up; most of what exists is humanitarian, localized, or indirect.

The strongest negative evidence comes from conflict-affected eastern DRC, so national-level welfare performance may be somewhat better outside those zones, but I did not find data strong enough to prove a broad improvement.","evidence":[{"title":"Democratic Republic of Congo: Expanding and Equipping Primary School Classrooms for Better Learning Outcomes","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-02-28","url":"https://www.worldbank.org/en/news/press-release/2024/02/28/democratic-republic-of-congo-afe-expanding-and-equipping-primary-school-classrooms-for-better-learning-outcomes","summary":"The PEQIP project was designed to improve primary education access and quality, add classrooms and learning materials, support students with disabilities, recruit better-qualified teachers, and address water/sanitation gaps in schools. This is strong positive evidence for 6B.2, but it is still a project announcement rather than proof of nationwide improvement.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.1"]},{"title":"Strengthening Public Social Spending in DRC","publisher":"IMF","date":"2024","url":"https://www.elibrary.imf.org/view/journals/002/2024/227/article-A002-en.xml","summary":"The IMF said social spending had increased, with education and health prioritized, and that free primary education had expanded access. It also said social protection remained very weak. This is positive evidence for a welfare-oriented policy direction, but only partial and uneven.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.1"]},{"title":"Democratic Republic of Congo: In the water sector, taking stock of challenges leads to new solutions","publisher":"World Bank","date":"2024-06-10","url":"https://connect4impact.worldbank.org/topic/democratic-republic-congo-water-sector-taking-stock-challenges-leads-new-solutions","summary":"The World Bank said DRC still had very low access to water and sanitation, but the new PASEA program launched with the government on 8 May 2024 aimed to expand basic drinking water and sanitation access in selected provinces. That is real positive evidence, though still localized and early-stage.","question_ids":["6B.2"]},{"title":"UNICEF cash transfers help build community resilience","publisher":"UNICEF DRC","date":"2024-06-18","url":"https://www.unicef.org/drcongo/en/stories/unicef-cash-transfers-help-build-community-resilience","summary":"UNICEF described humanitarian cash transfers as helping families eat more nutritiously, send children to school, and obtain needed health care, with explicit goals of reducing food insecurity, malnutrition, displacement, and barriers to health and education. This is positive evidence for social protection, but the initiative is limited in scale.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.1"]},{"title":"DRC: President Tshisekedi must use second term to tackle human rights crisis","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-06-24","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/06/drc-president-tshisekedi-must-use-second-term-to-tackle-human-rights-crisis/","summary":"Amnesty said public resources were being squandered, leaving essential services underfunded and preventing realization of rights to food, healthcare, water, sanitation, education, and housing. This is strong negative evidence that welfare was not being treated as the overriding purpose of rule.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.1"]},{"title":"DRC President Felix Tshisekedi must be held accountable for human rights violations","publisher":"Amnesty International","date":"2024-09-30","url":"https://www.amnesty.org/en/latest/news/2024/09/drc-president-felix-tshisekedi-must-be-held-accountable-for-human-rights-violations/","summary":"Amnesty said the humanitarian response was chronically underfunded and that urgent needs for shelter, food, healthcare, and education were still unmet, while the state of siege militarized daily life. This is strong negative evidence for welfare-first governance.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.1"]},{"title":"DR Congo: Second Term Should Focus on Rights","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024-03-06","url":"https://www.hrw.org/news/2024/03/06/dr-congo-second-term-should-focus-rights","summary":"HRW said corruption and repression reduced the government’s capacity to deliver quality education, health care, and social security, and that the administration had made little progress on systemic reform. This is negative evidence against a genuine welfare-centered governing model.","question_ids":["6B.2","6B.1"]},{"title":"Democratic Republic of Congo Battling Worsening Humanitarian Crisis, Armed Conflict, Despite Recent Peaceful Elections","publisher":"United Nations","date":"2024-03-27","url":"https://press.un.org/en/2024/sc15646.doc.htm","summary":"The UN said eastern Congo’s crisis had worsened, with massive displacement and acute hunger; it noted that one Congolese person in four faced hunger and malnutrition. That is strong evidence that food security and basic welfare were still deteriorating under Tshisekedi’s rule environment.","question_ids":["6B.2"]},{"title":"Democratic Republic of Congo: Humanitarian Situation Report No. 1, 30 June 2024","publisher":"UNICEF","date":"2024-06-30","url":"https://www.unicef.org/documents/democratic-republic-congo-humanitarian-situation-report-no-1-30-june-2024","summary":"UNICEF’s 2024 humanitarian reporting shows that conflict, displacement, and service disruption remained severe enough to require ongoing emergency response. This is negative context for access to health, education, WASH, and protection services.","question_ids":["6B.2"]}]}
